To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TileCal read-out driver system has been produced and is operating in the ATLAS experiment at CERN, with a good performance.

the ROD board is a 9 U VME board with 8 DSPs, the ROD board was tested during production with a set of tests that include the online algorithms and the performance of the algorithms was studied with data taken in the TileCal commissioning phase.
the ROD board has been successfully used to read out the TileCal detector during the commissioning of the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadtron Collider.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production, test and operation of the ROD boards for the TileCal calorimeters.
the development of a new generation of VLSI circuits for the implementation of high performance digital signal processing algorithms for the ATLAS hadronic calorimeter detector.

the design, production and initial performance of the TileCal ROD boards, which are the central element of the TileCal data processing system and which have been successfully installed in the ATLAS experiment.

the RODs are working properly and are fully operational.
the ROD boards have been successfully tested and the algorithms have performed as expected.
the TileCal ROD system was fully operational during the 2007-2008 LHC commissioning and the 2009 LHC pilot run.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TileCal detector has passed all its tests and is fully operational for the first physics runs at LHC.
the ROD boards were successfully produced and tested, and the performance of the algorithms implemented in the ROD boards is in line with the design requirements.
the production of ROD boards is completed and the first results from online algorithms have been successfully achieved.

the ROD boards are fully operational and that the performance of the algorithms is in good agreement with the expectations.
the ROD board has met all its performance requirements and that the algorithms used for data processing are ready to be run in the ATLAS experiment.
the ROD system meets the requirements of the ATLAS experiment.
